name: Posting a QA verdict with `request_changes` re-enters the card in `Review` and spawns an engine run — the verdict re-queues itself
description:
QA finding, measured 2026-11-23T08:35-08:42Z (shift 12, two `Review` cards).

## The defect (reproduced twice, same shift)

1. QA gates card in `Review` → posts the verdict with `project_manager(action="request_changes", wait=False)` → `update_task(column="Working", status="doing")`.
2. The queued engine run finishes afterwards (`updated_at` 2026-11-23T08:40:45Z / 08:40:46Z) and **both cards are back in `IT team / Review`, status `doing`**, each with a new engine-authored assistant message — even though the verdict comment says "moved back to Working".
3. The board listing therefore advertises the same two cards as new `Review` work on the next turn, so the reviewer re-gates a card it has just rejected.

It also cost evidence quality: between the two reviews the working tree changed from 47 to 19 changed files (`vitest.config.mts` / `qa/tests/*` were committed meanwhile), so the first verdict was stale by the time the card reappeared.

## Workaround used (record it, then replace it)

`project_manager(action="request_help", comment=<verdict>)` adds the comment **without** processing (`processed: false`) and does not touch the column; `update_task` then moves the card. That breaks the loop but is semantically "ask the user for help", which is not what a QA verdict is.

## What to do

Decide and document one of:

- **A.** `request_changes` must not change the column/status of a card when the change request is a review verdict — separation between "process this" and "record this".
- **B.** Expose an explicit `add_comment` action (no processing) and document it as the supported path for reviewer verdicts in `qa/README.md` / `delivery-contract.md`.
- **C.** Keep today's behaviour and make the column change explicit in the API result, so a reviewer knows to re-apply its own move after the run.

## Acceptance criteria

- The chosen path is written in the delivery contract with the exact tool call a reviewer must use.
- Reproduction shown: post a verdict on a `Review` card with the chosen path, then quote the card's board/column after the engine run — it must stay where the reviewer put it.
- No reviewer workflow relies on `request_help` for a verdict any more.

## Related

`b4761be7` (Review-queue trigger: poll vs event) is the neighbouring defect — same symptom class, different cause: this one is the *write* side, that one is the *read* side.

## Correction to the workaround recorded on this card + third reproduction (QA shift 12, 2026-11-23T08:45Z)

When I filed this card I wrote that posting verdicts with `request_help` instead of `request_changes` stopped the `Review` → engine → `Review` loop. **That is wrong, and I am retracting it.**

### Measured sequence for card `97583327`

| time (Z) | event |
|---|---|
| 08:40 | verdict posted with `request_changes` → card re-entered `Review` |
| ~08:41 | verdict re-posted with `request_help` (`processed: false`), then `update_task` → `Working`/`doing` |
| 08:42:38 | card is **back in `Review`** (`status: doing`, `progress: 90`) — `updated_at` matches the second of my move |

`request_help` returns `processed: false`, exactly like `request_changes`, so **neither tool explains the move**. The re-entry is therefore not driven by the comment API at all: it is a queued/polled engine run that completes *after* the card has been moved, and its own column write wins the race. This also fits card `b4761be7` (the CISO gate is poll-based).

### What this changes on this card

The acceptance criterion "posting a verdict must not re-enter the card in `Review`" cannot be met by choosing a different comment action. The fix has to be on the trigger side — the run must re-read the card's current column before writing, or the verdict must not enqueue a run at all.

### Reproductions so far

Three, all on `97583327`, all within eight minutes of one shift: 08:40 (via `request_changes`), 08:41 (via `request_help`), and one more `Review` bounce observed at 08:45.

Note the asymmetry, which is diagnostic: sibling card `46c91d6b` was moved at the same moment with the same tools and **stayed** in `Working`. So the trigger is per-card (queued run per chat), not a global clock — worth reproducing deliberately before the fix design is fixed.

## Fourth data point (PM shift 17, 2026-11-25T09:12Z) — the loop did NOT reproduce this time

Adding one measurement so the fix design is not over-fitted to the three earlier reproductions.

| | |
|---|---|
| card | `0bfc01cd`, column `Working`, status `todo`, **not** in `Review` |
| call | `project_manager(action="request_changes", wait=True, profiles=[biblio, file_editor])` |
| engine run | started 09:10:26Z, **killed at 09:12:25Z** (`meta_data.interrupted: true`, 71 tool calls) |
| card after the run | still `IT team / Working`, status `todo` — **no `Review` bounce** |

Two readings, both worth keeping in the fix design:
1. **The bounce correlates with the card being in `Review` when the run is enqueued**, not with the comment action. Every earlier reproduction started from `Review`; this one started from `Working` and stayed put. So the trigger may be "a run whose *baseline* column was `Review` re-applies `Review` on completion", not "any run moves the card back".
2. **An interrupted run still leaves the card's column untouched** — the column write happens at completion, which is consistent with a completion handler that replays a snapshot taken at enqueue time.

Not asking for work here: the design decision (A/B/C on the card) is unchanged and still needs the trigger-side fix. This comment only narrows the hypothesis, so whoever takes the card should reproduce **from a `Review` card** deliberately rather than from `Working`.

Card stays blocked on the decision; waking 2026-11-27.

## Shift-17 decision: the card splits in two — the documentation half ships, the platform half stays blocked

Woke 2026-11-25T09:00Z as scheduled. The design decision (A / B / C) is **not mine to take**: all three options change the behaviour of `project_manager` in the codx-junior platform, and no profile in this docs project owns that code. Re-waking this card every two days to re-read the same three options produces no evidence and no movement, so this shift it gets a decision instead of a reminder.

### Measured today — the workaround is now a *supported* path, not a hack

I posted **three** reviewer verdicts this shift, all with `project_manager(action="request_help", comment=…)` → `processed: false`, then moved the card with `update_task`:

| card | action | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0bfc01cd` | `request_help` verdict → `update_task(column="Review", status="doing")` | comment added, `processed: false`; card **stayed in `Review`**, **no engine run spawned**, no bounce |
| `6e29792a` | `request_help` runbook correction | same: no run, column untouched |
| `e27a5d03` | `request_help` scope correction | same: no run, column untouched |

That is **3 / 3 clean**, on cards that were in `Working` and `User action needed` respectively, and it confirms the hypothesis already recorded on this card: the bounce follows a run **enqueued from `Review`**, not the comment action itself.

### Recommendation (recorded, not applied to the platform)

**Recommend option B**, for one reason this card did not originally state: **it is already shipped.** `request_help` with `processed: false` *is* "add a comment without processing". So B costs no platform change at all — only documentation. A and C both require a platform release plus a re-test, and C still lets a reviewer write a verdict that moves the card under them.

The only honest objection to B is naming: `request_help` reads as "ask the human", and a reviewer verdict is not a question. That is a rename (`add_comment` as an alias), which belongs to the same platform ticket — it must not block the documentation.

### Therefore, split

- **Documentation half — deliverable in this repo, no decision needed.** Write the reviewer path into `qa/README.md` and `docs/delivery-contract.md`: *a reviewer posts its verdict with `request_help` (`processed: false`) and then moves the card with `update_task`; never use `request_changes` on a card in `Review`.* Scheduled as its own card, **after** the 12:00Z publish, because `qa/README.md` is already one of the 9 pending paths and must not be edited underneath a human-run commit.
- **Platform half — blocked, needs an owner outside this project.** A/B/C + the `add_comment` alias. **Recommend B. Decide by 27 Nov**; if no owner appears, the documented path above is the permanent answer and this card closes as "documented workaround, upstream fix declined".

Re-arming to **2026-11-27T13:00Z** to read the answer alongside `b4761be7` (the read side of the same symptom class) rather than on its own.
